definitions.explanation: A document summarizing one's personal information, education, and work history for job applications.

examples.japanese: {履歴書|りれきしょ}を{書|か}いて{送|おく}った。
examples.english: I wrote a resume and sent it.

examples.japanese: {履歴書|りれきしょ}には{写真|しゃしん}を{貼|は}ってください。
examples.english: Please attach a photo to your resume.

examples.japanese: {履歴書|りれきしょ}は{手書|てが}きで{書|か}いた{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: It's better to write your resume by hand.

notes:
{履歴書|りれきしょ} is a compound: {履歴|りれき} (personal history) + {書|しょ} (document).

JAPANESE RESUME FORMAT:
Japanese {履歴書|りれきしょ} follows a standardized format (JIS規格) that includes:
- {写真|しゃしん} (photo - required)
- {学歴|がくれき} (educational background)
- {職歴|しょくれき} (work history)
- {志望動機|しぼうどうき} (reason for applying)
- {趣味|しゅみ}・{特技|とくぎ} (hobbies/special skills)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {履歴書|りれきしょ}を{書|か}く (to write a resume)
- {履歴書|りれきしょ}を{送|おく}る (to send a resume)
- {履歴書|りれきしょ}を{提出|ていしゅつ}する (to submit a resume)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally, Japanese resumes are handwritten, as handwriting is thought to reveal personality. However, typed resumes are becoming more acceptable, especially in modern industries.
